$comment: Release binary trust anchors. This file is a COMMITTED, REVIEWED WITNESS -
it must never be generated by the same build that consumes it.
The defect this replaces: apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs computed
EMBEDDED_RELEASE_HASHES by hashing resources/aether.exe - the very file it
then shipped - so the runtime comparison could only ever succeed, and on a
clean checkout (where resources/*.exe is gitignored) it hashed nothing,
emitted no entry, and the 'missing digest is an error' guard was
unreachable. Both directions of that check were unable to fail.
Lifecycle: prepare-anchor builds an unsigned engine, records its SHA-256 and
workflow artifact pointer, then opens a pull request. The release downloads
those exact bytes. The desktop checks the embedded digest before spawning it.
Correction on record: this entry originally read
e5da74c1d10af92eb2022963f56af085390f000da6c0c02b7ea35fe5b0b2afce, which is not
the digest of packaging/wintun.dll (e5da8447dc2c320edc0fc52fa01885c103de8c118481f683643cacc3220dafce,
which is also what .github/workflows/build.yml pins). A hand-written anchor that
was never compared against the artifact it describes is how a correct file ends up
refused and an incorrect one accepted; every value here now comes from a measured digest.
Field meanings: file_sha256 is sha256 over the artifact's bytes. The engine is
unsigned and has no cert_sha256 or issued_cn. The vendor-signed WinTUN driver
retains its certificate pin and subject. An all-zero file_sha256 means no
witness has been published yet: a release build then refuses that artifact with
anchor_not_published rather than pretending the comparison succeeded.
Three further fields describe provenance rather than content, and scripts/package-policy.mjs
reads them before any package is called distributable. The engine profile is
unsigned-witnessed after review; the driver profile is trusted-ca. witnessed_run
and witnessed_artifact name the prepare-anchor run whose bytes
file_sha256 describes - the release job downloads exactly that artifact and never rebuilds
or re-signs the engine, because a second signing of a second compilation cannot produce
the same bytes and the hash check would then be a formality that only ever fails.
Entries stay FLAT objects: scripts/publish-engine-trust.mjs locates an entry with a
no-braces regex, so a nested object in here silently becomes an entry it cannot find.
